title: Accessibility/UDL + age-appropriateness checklists
context: Because lesson plans produced by this project are intended for real classrooms with children, every plan must meet two non-negotiable quality bars: (1) accessibility and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) — differentiation for varied readiness, language supports for multilingual learners, plain language, alt-text for images, and screen-reader-friendly structure; and (2) age-appropriateness, inclusivity, and safeguarding — non-discriminatory, non-partisan content suited to the stated grade band. Without a concrete, committed checklist for both, plan authors and reviewers have no shared standard to apply. This task creates those checklists, which will be enforced by the pedagogy/standards reviewer gate and later automated in the reading-level/sensitive-subject detector (task-010).
objective: Create the Accessibility/UDL checklist and the age-appropriateness/inclusivity/safeguarding checklist that every lesson plan must satisfy before publication, and establish the protocol for sensitive-subject escalation to medium risk.
acceptanceCriteria: Accessibility/UDL checklist covers at minimum: plain-language writing for the stated grade band, alt-text required for any image or visual element, screen-reader-friendly document structure, differentiation section with support[], extension[], and languageSupports[], and udlNotes capturing Universal Design for Learning rationale.

Age-appropriateness checklist covers: content is appropriate for the stated grade band (verified against a recognized readability/developmental framework), no discriminatory, stereotyping, or exclusionary content, non-partisan treatment of contested civic/political/religious/cultural topics, and inclusive example names/scenarios (fictional).

Safeguarding checklist covers: no collection or inclusion of real student or teacher PII, sensitive-subject identification (health, safety, sexuality, religion, contested history/politics), and mandatory escalation path for any sensitive subject to riskTier: medium with subject-expert review.
The sensitive-subject escalation protocol specifies: which topics trigger escalation, what 'education, not advice' framing means and requires, and that escalation is mandatory (not optional).
Checklists are structured as enumerated yes/no items that a plan author self-checks and the pedagogy/standards reviewer verifies.
Document is committed to the repo and serves as the normative reference for plan-authoring tasks and for the readability/sensitive-subject detector (teacher-lesson-plans-readability-010).
resources: PLAN.md — §Data, licensing & compliance (Safeguarding & content standards section)
teacher-lesson-plans-template-001 — canonical schema (differentiation, accessibility, sensitiveSubject fields)
Universal Design for Learning (UDL) guidelines — https://udlguidelines.cast.org/
output: A committed document containing: the Accessibility/UDL checklist, the age-appropriateness/inclusivity/safeguarding checklist, and the sensitive-subject escalation protocol — all as enumerated, verifiable items ready for plan authors and reviewers to apply.
